meta.description: Curated country-level citizenship acquisition rules. The four top-level modes are ancestry, naturalization, birth, and investment. This file stores reviewed records; scripts/build_citizenship_routes.js expands them over the complete jurisdiction registry.
meta.scope: Incremental verified slice: education-residence credit rules for France and Colombia; selected nationality routes for Portugal, Malta, Bulgaria, and Greece; active direct citizenship-by-investment programmes; ended programmes where a stale recommendation would be harmful; and explicit pending records where a statutory basis exists but present operation is unclear.

routes.title: French higher education can reduce the naturalization residence period to two years
routes.summary: French Civil Code article 21-17 ordinarily requires five years of habitual residence and does not exclude lawful student residence. Article 21-18 reduces that period to two years for a person who successfully completes two years of higher education toward a diploma from a French university or higher-education institution. A valid permit, continuing residence, assimilation, language and stable professional integration remain material; naturalization is discretionary.

facts.reduction_condition: Successfully complete two years of higher education toward a diploma from a French university or higher-education institution

routes.title: Visitor student visa time does not accumulate toward permanent residence
routes.summary: Colombia's current student route is a Visitor (V) visa. The Foreign Ministry states that study time does not count toward a Resident (R) visa by accumulated time; article 90 lists qualifying Migrant (M) categories and does not include the V student visa.

sources.title: Colombia Foreign Ministry — V Student Visa

routes.title: Investor citizenship criteria
routes.summary: Jordan's Cabinet-approved criteria, administered by the Ministry of Investment / Invest Jordan, provide citizenship routes through qualifying securities, productive projects, business expansion or sustained job creation. Several project routes require a multi-year compliance period, often with a temporary three-year passport before a recommendation for full citizenship. Dual nationality is routinely permitted on this economic pathway.

sources.title: Invest Jordan — Cabinet investor residency and citizenship criteria
Jordan News Agency (Petra) — Cabinet investor citizenship amendments

routes.title: Ordinary naturalization uses seven- or ten-year residence periods under the 2026 law
routes.summary: For applications made from 19 May 2026, the ordinary legal-residence period is seven years for nationals of Portuguese-speaking countries and EU Member States, and ten years for other nationals. Applications already pending when the law entered into force remain under the earlier rules. The Ministry of Justice notes that some practical implementation still requires supplementary regulation; eligibility is not an automatic grant.

sources.title: Portuguese Ministry of Justice — Nationality Law: new rules effective 19 May
Portuguese Ministry of Justice — Portuguese nationality

routes.title: Birth in Portugal can qualify when a parent has five years of legal residence
routes.summary: The 2026 nationality-law changes provide a birth-in-Portugal route where, at the time of birth, one parent has legally resided in Portugal for at least five years. This is a conditional jus soli rule, not unconditional citizenship for every child born in Portugal; additional statutory conditions and implementation rules must be checked for an individual case.

sources.title: Portuguese Ministry of Justice — Nationality Law: new rules effective 19 May

routes.title: Residence-based naturalization requires the final twelve months plus four of the preceding six years
routes.summary: An adult may apply after residing in Malta throughout the twelve months immediately before the application and for an aggregate of at least four years during the preceding six years. The applicant must also meet character and language requirements. Naturalization remains a ministerial, discretionary decision rather than an entitlement after five calendar years.

sources.title: Community Malta Agency — Acquisition of Citizenship

routes.title: Registration routes cover defined descent and family connections
routes.summary: Registration in the direct line requires two consecutive ascendants born in Malta. Act XXI of 2025 moved the governing date in articles 3 and 5 from 2007/2010 to 1 August 2028: an ascendant who dies before that date is deemed to have acquired citizenship, while a parent alive on it must themselves have acquired Maltese citizenship under the article for the claim to pass. A foreign spouse may register after five years of marriage. Every grant requires the Minister to be satisfied it is not contrary to the public interest.

sources.title: Community Malta Agency — Acquisition of Citizenship
Maltese Citizenship (Amendment) Act, Act XXI of 2025

routes.title: The former transactional investor-citizenship programme has ended
routes.summary: Malta discontinued the Granting of Citizenship for Exceptional Services programme following the Court of Justice of the European Union judgment, and Act XXI of 2025 then deleted the "individual investor programme" definition from the Act entirely. The substituted article 10(9) grants merit naturalisation for exceptional service or contribution, including through job creation, naming scientists, athletes, artists, entrepreneurs, philanthropists and technologists among the qualifying categories. It sets no financial threshold and must not be represented as a citizenship-by-investment product.

sources.title: Government of Malta — citizenship programme discontinued
Community Malta Agency — amendments to the Citizenship Act
Community Malta Agency — naturalisation on the basis of merit
Maltese Citizenship (Amendment) Act, Act XXI of 2025

routes.title: Ordinary naturalization generally requires five years holding permanent or long-term residence
routes.summary: Bulgaria's ordinary route generally requires an adult to have held permanent or long-term residence for at least five years, alongside criminal-record, income or occupation, Bulgarian-language and—unless an exception applies—prior-citizenship release requirements. This is five years after the qualifying residence status, not a promise of citizenship after five years of any lawful stay.

sources.title: Bulgarian Ministry of Justice — Bulgarian Citizenship Act, article 12
Bulgarian Ministry of Justice — Bulgarian citizenship services

routes.title: Bulgarian-origin route can waive residence, income, language and renunciation conditions
routes.summary: A person of Bulgarian origin may apply under article 15 without the ordinary residence, income, language and release-of-prior-citizenship conditions. The applicant must establish the family relationship with at least one ancestor of Bulgarian origin, up to the third degree inclusive, using the required official documents.

sources.title: Bulgarian Ministry of Justice — Bulgarian Citizenship Act, article 15

routes.title: Investor-citizenship provisions were repealed in 2022
routes.summary: Bulgaria repealed the special investment-based citizenship provisions in 2022. Investment or property ownership should not be presented as a current direct route to Bulgarian citizenship; any residence obtained on another legal basis follows the applicable ordinary nationality rules.

sources.title: National Assembly of Bulgaria — investment citizenship provisions repealed
Bulgarian Ministry of Justice — Bulgarian Citizenship Act

routes.title: Ordinary naturalization generally requires seven years of legal residence

Applicants must also satisfy the applicable integration, language, civic-knowledge and character requirements; residence eligibility is not an automatic grant.

routes.title: Citizenship routes exist through a Greek parent and defined descent declarations
routes.summary: Greek nationality law provides acquisition and declaration procedures for people born to a Greek parent, with separate documentary routes depending on birth date, registration and the parents' marital or acknowledgment status. This record confirms the route family but does not collapse those distinct procedures into one universal checklist.

routes.title: Citizenship by birth in the United States
routes.summary: The Fourteenth Amendment Citizenship Clause and 8 U.S.C. § 1401 grant citizenship at birth to a person born in the United States and subject to its jurisdiction. Traditional exceptions include children of foreign diplomats (and related extraterritorial fictions), not a parental-status test. Executive Order 14160 (20 January 2025) sought to deny citizenship to children of parents unlawfully or temporarily present; the Supreme Court held in Trump v. Barbara (25-365, 30 June 2026) that such children remain subject to U.S. jurisdiction and are citizens at birth. Unconditional jus soli for birth-tourism purposes remains the law.

sources.title: Supreme Court — Trump v. Barbara (25-365), 30 June 2026

routes.title: Dominican nationality by birth in the Dominican Republic
routes.summary: Persons born in the national territory are Dominican under Article 18, except children of foreign diplomats and of foreigners in transit or illegally present as defined by Dominican law.

routes.title: Nationality by birth in Chile

routes.title: Citizenship at birth in Pakistan

routes.title: Uruguayan nationality by territorial birth

routes.title: Citizenship by birth in Antigua and Barbuda
